description: Long open-top steel roll-off container with a hook bar at the front and hinged rear doors, dropped behind sites and condos

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Long open-topped steel refuse container standing on two full-length skid rails, its four sides plain flat panels stiffened by broad vertical ribs pressed down them and finished with a thick rolled rim all the way round the open top, the front end wall rising higher than the sides into a tall flat headboard with a single stout curved hook bar standing proud of it at mid height, the rear end a pair of tall flat doors filling the whole end with heavy strap hinges down their outer edges and one long horizontal locking bar across them, small solid roller wheels at the two back corners Materials: Faded orange-brown industrial enamel worn through to bare steel along every rib and rim, heavy scale rust across the lower panels and up from the skids, dried grey cement splashes and dark leachate streaks down the outside, mud caked on the skid rails, stencilled numbers ghosted on the headboard.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless pure WHITE studio matte. The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless white backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91. 1,760/2,000 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 1/2 materials, 2/4 unique geometries, one 512 px canvas at 1.3 MB and a 61 ms factory. Turntable gate 0 enclosed background pixels at all four azimuths.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope 1.44 x 1.50 x 1.98 m, measured 1.440 x 1.500 x 1.982. Band table against the Meshy proxy: mean |delta width| 0.0063, |delta depth| 0.0147, every band within 0.034 of HEIGHT -- band 9 (the flange) +0.003 / -0.006, bands 3-7 (the walls) within 0.015, band 0 (the skid rails) -0.005. The same table read 0.347 / 1.352 against the uncorrected 1.9 x 1.5 x 3.9 declaration.
featureReviews.notes: The declaration was corrected before the rebuild, not scored around.

featureReviews.evidence: No lid at any azimuth. The walls are 0.035 m plate so their inside faces exist, and separate 0.007-0.008 m liners in a darker tone (#ce7241) give the interior its own value; the floor is visible from above at 0, 90, 180, 270 and the hero. The rear is left OPEN in the shell and closed by the leaves, so opening a door reveals the interior rather than a fourth wall.
featureReviews.notes: Nothing stands on the floor: the plate shows the rim from above and no contents.

featureReviews.evidence: A recessed field inside a proud border frame on all four elevations, with two stiffener ribs a side and a mid-rail on the headboard; four corner posts, kick rails, and a border frame plus central rib on BOTH faces of each leaf. The proud families sit in four separate planes (posts 0.690 from centre, frames 0.678, kick rails 0.670, ribs 0.666), the flange rails butt rather than overlap, and the frame rails butt their stiles: check-coplanar reports clean at 0.001 m.

Two I-section skid rails at x +-0.50 running the full 1.72 m and standing the body clear of the ground; three cross members; four rollers r 0.072 on stub axles with hub caps; the hook bar r 0.036 x 0.64 standing 0.036 m proud of two brackets on the headboard, on raked gussets. The rails were a low channel first, which left a 0.09 m open slot the turntable gate found 663 background pixels in; taking them full height closed it and moved band 0 from -0.085 to -0.005.
featureReviews.notes: The hook bar and headboard are on the one end the single plate never shows and are authored from the asset description at confidence 0.70, recorded as region-headboard rather than presented as observed.

featureReviews.evidence: Two leaves on door-hinge-l and door-hinge-r at the rear corner posts, each with border frames both faces, two strap hinges with knuckles and bolt heads, and a cam bar with two keepers, two end collars and a cranked D-handle. The second instance is ROLLED 180 degrees about Z, not yawed: a yaw maps local +z to world -z and puts every fitting inside the container, which is the fault this asset's own first review records, and an InstancedMesh cannot mirror.
featureReviews.notes: That the doors are on the SHORT rear end is an assumption at confidence 0.62. Three perspective reads of the plate -- top-face edge directions, per-corner distance ratios 1.210 against 1.119, and the skid rails' image slope of -0.32 matching the door face's -0.375 rather than the long face's +0.16 -- put the plate's doors on the LONG side. Overridden because a generated plate is routinely projectively inconsistent and the asset contract names rear hinges.

featureReviews.evidence: One 512 px canvas re-basing the envelope to #e98d5a (linear K 1.000 / 1.299 / 1.822) and multiplying back to clean #e97d43, with rust #dd6d2d in clustered granular patches and runs, chalk bloom #d18d5a, and paint grain; height-keyed at 1.55 m so rust bleeds down from the top rail and a grime band darkens the base. Both weathering tones are plate-measured RATIOS against clean paint in the same light, (0.949, 0.874, 0.673) and (0.898, 1.126, 1.345), carried onto the shipped paint rather than pasted as the pixels they were sampled from.
featureReviews.notes: The chalk ratio exceeds 1 in green and blue, so a plain multiply could not reach it; the re-base is what makes the bloom possible at all. One material, so the iron hardware shares the paint's roughness response -- the second draw call went to the doors, which need it more.

name: Hook-Lift Roll-Off Skip
nameTh: ตู้คอนเทนเนอร์ขยะ
notes: The hook-lift container a truck backs under and drags aboard on its rails -- dropped behind construction sites, condo builds, factories and hotel service yards. Open-topped by design: no lid at all, which is the clearest silhouette difference from the lidded municipal steel bin, and means the interior floor and the inside faces of the walls are visible from above and have to exist. Two full-length skid rails and the hook bar on the front headboard are what identify it; without them it is just a large box. Rear doors hinge on the outer edges of the back end, so it ships a root pivot plus door-hinge-l and door-hinge-r on the rear corner posts and no sockets. Not breakable. Static and physics disabled: an empty one weighs most of a tonne and a full one is immovable, so it is level furniture rather than something a player pushes. SIZE CORRECTED 2026-08-31, from 1.9 x 1.5 x 3.9: the list-time estimate described a 6 cubic metre roll-off and the plate does not show one. The Meshy proxy's raw bbox is 1.897 x 1.480 x 1.407, H-normalised 1.282 / 1.000 / 0.951, and scratch/_mon/bands.mjs at 5-95 pct reads w/h 0.85 and d/h 1.19 against the then-shipped model's 1.21 / 2.55 -- a mean depth error of 1.35 of HEIGHT, the largest single defect in that build. An independent projective read of the plate agrees: the two visible faces project to 1.066 m and 1.046 m at equal scale, which for a rectangular box puts d/w near 1.4, not the declared 2.05. Anchored on the declared 1.50 m height (unchanged, and the primary axis), that gives a shell of 1.28 x 1.79 and a top flange of 1.44 x 1.92 -- both within 0.03 H of the proxy in every band -- and a declared 1.44 x 1.50 x 1.98 once the hook bar (front, -0.996 m) and the door cam handles (rear, +0.986 m) are counted, two fittings on ends the single plate never shows and the proxy never reconstructed. Rebuilt against the corrected envelope the band table reads mean |delta width| 0.0066 and |delta depth| 0.0145. COLLIDER CEILING: budgetClass is pinned back to large after the size correction derived medium, and the four RENDER ceilings are pinned to medium's own numbers (2000 / 2 / 2 / 4) as per-asset overrides so the prop claims no frame time the size rule says it has not earned. The class is doing one job here: colliderPartCeiling() reads budgetClass alone, and medium allows 4 parts. This is an OPEN-TOP vessel, so at 4 parts the derivation merges the front and rear wall slabs into one block filling the interior -- volumeRatio 3.585 and 67% of the footprint standing 1.2 m above the real floor, which promote correctly refuses. At 8 it derives the hollow shell the prop actually is: four wall slabs, the floor and the two skid rails, coverage 0.9932, overshoot 0.000, p95 0.002 m, volumeRatio 1.389. The parts are affordable because physics.enabled is false -- they are broad-phase only, and the halving colliderPartCeiling applies to dynamic bodies does not bite.
